First Aid, CPR certification (Preferred)
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.

Minimum 4 years of experience handling animals while facilitating learning experiences with species similar to the current colony of Animal Discovery Zone animals (reptiles, amphibians, mammals, and arthropods), including thorough subject area knowledge of exotic animal natural history and ethology, as well as basic knowledge of appropriate species-specific behavior and it's relationship to animal health
Minimum 4 years professional experience with animal husbandry, including creating museum-quality live animal habitat displays and lighting
Minimum 2 years of experience facilitating and developing informal educational programs focused on ecology, conservation, zoology and/or related fields of the life sciences
Experience managing and training animal care staff, volunteers, and professional educators to help facilitate program activities with diverse audiences

Functional knowledge of informal educational techniques including the ability to deliver developmentally appropriate and effective pedagogy to engage diverse learners in experiences, programs, and exhibitions

Under the general supervision of the Senior Museum Scientist, the Living Collections Specialist supports the curation and maintenance of the live animal ambassador colony used in educational programs and demonstrations at The Lawrence Hall of Science's Animal Discovery Zone. This position collaborates with University partners and other departments to plan, develop, and lead programs that enhance the public's understanding of the life sciences and STEM education. The Living Collections Specialist provides work direction and mentors UC Berkeley student assistants and volunteers on the animal care team and provides administrative and operational support to the Senior Museum Scientist to ensure a high quality of life for the animal ambassador colony.
Operations, Staff & Administrative Support - 35%
Create the monthly student staff schedule
Provide work direction for and mentor student staff in their animal husbandry and facilitation duties
Support training and hiring processes
Manage inventory, records, task delegation, and operational problem-solving; purchase supplies as needed
Animal Care & Health Management - 30%
Develop and oversee schedule of species-specific diet plans, feeding, grooming, enrichment, health monitoring and medications
Collaborate with veterinary staff as needed
Create and maintain SOPs, task schedules, cleaning protocols, and educational guides for animal care staff and volunteers
Habitat Design & Environmental Management - 20%
Create species-appropriate enclosure parameters that promote natural behaviors and provide visually engaging experiences for visitors
Oversee routine cleaning and maintenance schedule for animal enclosures
Collaboration & Public Engagement - 15%
Cross-departmental collaboration, event participation, public outreach, and educational programming
Occasionally facilitate engaging programs with the public

Commitment to teamworkcontributes to achieving group goals; supports teams efforts to succeed; balances team and individual responsibilities; willing to adjust schedules for the team; completes tasks on time; takes responsibility for own actions; reliable

Possess ability to understand, interpret and extrapolate applicable information from reliable resources and research studies on best animal care practices and ethology, and make recommendations based on findings, demonstrating organizational and problem-solving skills
Possess knowledge at a college level of science (biology or conservation and resource studies preferred)

Positive public service attitude and the ability to establish rapport with diverse public science center visitors, staff and volunteers and create an inclusive and engaging learning environment for all

Excellent interpersonal skillsconsiders and responds appropriately to the needs and capabilities of different people in different situations; is tactful and treats others with respect; relates effectively to others when encountering difficult situations
Thorough and effective verbal, written, interpersonal communication and public speaking skills
Computer Skills with business software systems and database software in the completion of work assignments (for example, Microsoft Office Suite and Google Workspaces)
Work one weekend day a week (either SundayThursday or TuesdaySaturday). Ability to work evenings and some holidays as needed
Physical ability to pick up and carry supplies (up to 50 pounds)
Possess strong organizational skills
